name: supply-test-kits
narrative: Hauwa has to buy chlorine test kits to a specification she did not write, and today that specification lives in an emailed PDF nobody checks a quote against. She opens the test kit, picks Range maximum from the figures the catalogue already knows, and records the requirement Aqualytic cares most about: the kit must still read at the 2 mg/L dispenser dose. Harmattan Health Supplies, the distributor, has quoted two kits with the same fifty reagent tablets and comparator. Side by side, per test and per kit, the cheaper Brightwell kit ranks first, and its row says it fails one of Aqualytic's three requirements: its range stops at 1.5 mg/L. Hauwa awards the Lumen kit that meets all three requirements, and writes down why. She asks Aqualytic, as the technical partner, to confirm the Lumen kit meets AQ-TK-1 before anything is bought. Place order is disabled: the order waits on Aqualytic's answer, and the page says so. Hauwa sends Aqualytic a private update link to that one question. On Update links it sits beside Harmattan's standing link to everything Harmattan supplies. Kemi at Aqualytic opens the link with no labs login, approves the Lumen kit in her own words, and uploads her signed confirmation. Back on the award, Aqualytic's approval reads as given through its own link, with the signed letter beside it, and Place order, disabled until now, is live. Hauwa places the order on the terms Harmattan quoted: twenty kits, delivered at place to its Kano warehouse. Ibrahim at Harmattan opens Harmattan's own link, which already covers the new order, confirms it, and when the kits reach the Kano warehouse records twenty received. Hauwa opens the stock: Harmattan's warehouse holds twenty kits, a thousand tests, of the Lumen kit that meets AQ-TK-1 and that Aqualytic approved.
